models.job: The one that lives in the boot.
models.intro: Minu V3 is UPPAbaby's compact stroller. It folds one-handed to about the size of a carry-on, stands on its own, and is ready from birth as sold with the included infant insert. It is the pram for families who move a lot, live with stairs or a small boot, and want one stroller that covers the newborn stage and the toddler years without being a full-size pram.
models.facts: Minu V3 (stroller); 7.6 kg; folds to 25 x 45 x 55 cm; up to 1; works from birth; basket None kg

models.job: Not a full size pram. More than a travel pram.
models.intro: Kona is the mid-size pram in the UPPAbaby range. It has a reversible, from-birth seat and a full-size basket, but a slim footprint that clears a shop aisle and turns a tight corner. It suits parents who do not want the bulk of a full-size pram but need more than a travel stroller can carry.
models.facts: Kona (pram); 9.9 kg; folds to 34.0 x 53.3 x 65.5 cm; up to 1; works from birth; basket 13.6 kg

models.job: The everyday single, without the bulk.
models.intro: Cruz V3 is the full-size single pram. It has the same seat quality, canopy and basket as Vista in a narrower, lighter frame, and it is suitable from birth with the included infant insert. Cruz is for one child at a time: it does not take a second seat. Choose it over Vista when you are confident one child is the plan, or when boot space matters more than the option to add a sibling later.
models.facts: Cruz V3 (pram); up to 1; works from birth; basket None kg

models.job: Two children, side by side, through a standard doorway.
models.intro: Minu Duo is a side-by-side double stroller narrow enough to pass through a standard 73 cm doorway. Both seats are the same size, both recline, and both are usable from birth, which is unusual in a double this compact. It is the answer for twins, or for two children close in age, when a tandem is too long and a full double is too wide.
models.facts: Minu Duo (stroller); folds to 33 x 70.6 x 60.2 cm; up to 2; works from birth; basket 11.3 kg

models.job: For the trails and the long runs.
models.intro: Ridge V2 is the all-terrain jogger. Never-flat tyres, a locking front wheel and a long wheelbase make it stable at running pace and on gravel, sand and grass. It is the largest pram in the range folded, so it suits families with boot space who want one pram that handles a run and a beach track as easily as a footpath.
models.facts: Ridge V2 (pram); 13.7 kg; folds to 49.5 x 65 x 91.4 cm; up to 2; works from birth; basket None kg

models.job: One pram, up to three children.
models.intro: Vista V3 is the full-size pram built to grow with a family rather than a child. It ships with the bassinet included, so it is ready from birth out of the box, and it converts to carry two children with a RumbleSeat or a second bassinet, or three with a PiggyBack board. More than thirty configurations come off the one frame. It is the most expensive pram in the range and the only one that can absorb a second and third child without being replaced.
models.facts: Vista V3 (pram); up to 3; works from birth; basket 13.6 kg

faq.q: Can I use the Vista V3 from birth?
faq.a: Yes, straight out of the box. The bassinet is included, not an accessory you add later, so a newborn can lie flat on day one. The toddler seat takes over at around six months.

faq.q: How many children can a Vista V3 carry?
faq.a: Up to three on the one frame. Two seated, using a RumbleSeat or a second bassinet, and a third standing on a PiggyBack board that clips to the rear axle.

faq.q: Will a Vista V3 fit in my boot?
faq.a: Folded with the toddler seat attached it is {vista.folded}. With the seat removed it drops to {vista.folded_no_seat}. Measure the shortest side of your boot opening, not the space inside it. The opening is what stops a pram going in.

faq.q: How heavy is the Vista V3?
faq.a: {vista.weight} with the frame and toddler seat together. The frame alone is 9 kg, the seat 3.5 kg and the bassinet 4.2 kg, so it can be lifted in parts.

faq.q: Does the Mesa capsule fit the Vista V3?
faq.a: Yes, directly. The Mesa clicks onto the frame with no adapters, so a sleeping baby goes from the car to the pram without being unbuckled. Maxi-Cosi, Nuna, Joie and BeSafe capsules fit with the Vista upper car seat adapter.

faq.q: What is included in the box?
faq.a: Pram frame, toddler seat, bassinet, bumper bar, seasonal seat liner, toddler seat bug shield, toddler seat rain shield, bassinet bug shield, storage bag and the three year warranty. Nothing on that list is sold separately.

faq.q: How much can the basket hold?
faq.a: {vista.basket}, which is the largest in the range. It is reachable from either side, including when the seat faces you.

faq.q: Does the seat face me or face out?
faq.a: Both. The toddler seat is reversible, so it can face you while they are small and face forward when they would rather watch the world.
{vista.colours} for the Vista V3. Every one is the same pram underneath. What changes is the fabric, the frame finish and the leather.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Vista V3 and the Cruz V3?
faq.a: The Vista takes a second and a third child; the Cruz carries one and no accessory changes that. The Vista also includes the bassinet, where the Cruz needs one bought separately. The Cruz is narrower, lighter and less expensive.

faq.q: How wide is the Vista V3 when it is open?
faq.a: {vista.width} across, which is the figure that matters for shop aisles and front doors. Opened out it is {vista.unfolded}.

faq.q: Can I use the Cruz V3 from birth?
faq.a: Yes. It is suitable from birth as sold, using the included infant insert. A bassinet attaches directly to the frame if you would rather have a newborn lying flat, and it is sold separately.

faq.q: Can the Cruz V3 carry two children?
faq.a: No. The Cruz takes one child and no accessory changes that. If a second child is likely, the Vista V3 is the frame that absorbs one without being replaced.

faq.q: Will a Cruz V3 fit in my boot?
faq.a: Folded with the seat attached it is {cruz.folded}. With the seat removed it drops to {cruz.folded_no_seat}. Measure the opening of your boot rather than the space inside it.

faq.q: How heavy is the Cruz V3?
faq.a: {cruz.weight} with the frame and seat together. The frame alone is 7.7 kg and the seat 4.3 kg, so it lifts into a boot in two manageable pieces.

faq.q: Does the Mesa capsule fit the Cruz V3?
faq.a: Yes, directly, with no adapters. Other brands, including Maxi-Cosi, Nuna, Joie and BeSafe, fit using the same upper car seat adapter that covers Vista and Alta.

faq.q: How is the Cruz V3 different from the Vista V3?
faq.a: Same seat quality, canopy and basket, in a narrower and lighter frame that costs less. The trade is that the Cruz carries one child and the bassinet is not included.

faq.q: Does the seat face me or face out?
faq.a: Both. The seat is reversible and reclines flat enough for a newborn with the insert fitted.

faq.q: How much can the basket hold?
faq.a: The same generous basket as the Vista, reachable from either side including with the seat parent-facing.
{cruz.colours} for the Cruz V3, all the same pram underneath.

faq.q: How wide is the Cruz V3?
faq.a: {cruz.width} across, opened out to {cruz.unfolded}. That width is what clears a shop aisle and a standard front door.

faq.q: Can I add a ride-along board for an older child?
faq.a: Yes. The Cruz PiggyBack board clips to the rear axle for a child to stand on, and folds up when nobody is riding.

faq.q: Can I use the Minu V3 from birth?
faq.a: Yes, as sold. The infant insert is included, so it is a from-birth stroller rather than a six-months-and-up one, which is unusual at this size.

faq.q: Will a Minu V3 fit in my boot?
faq.a: Almost certainly. Folded it is {minu.folded}, which is around carry-on size and the smallest fold in the UPPAbaby range.

faq.q: How heavy is the Minu V3?
faq.a: {minu.weight}, the lightest pram we sell. In its box it is 9.4 kg, which matters if you are checking it as luggage.

faq.q: Does the Minu V3 fold one-handed?
faq.a: Yes, and it stands on its own once folded, so it does not need a wall to lean against on a train platform or in a hotel room.

faq.q: Does the Mesa capsule fit the Minu V3?
faq.a: Yes, with the Minu V3 capsule adapter, which is sold separately. It does not click on directly the way it does on a Vista or a Cruz.

faq.q: Can the Minu V3 carry two children?
faq.a: No. It is a single. For two side by side in a stroller this compact, the Minu Duo is the one: same family, two seats, still through a standard doorway.

faq.q: Is the Minu V3 seat reversible?
faq.a: No, the seat faces forward only. That is part of how the fold gets this small. If you want a parent-facing seat, look at the Cruz V3 or the Vista V3.

faq.q: How wide is the Minu V3?
faq.a: {minu.width} across, opened out to {minu.unfolded}. It is the narrowest pram in the range.

faq.q: Is the Minu V3 suitable as an only pram?
faq.a: For a lot of families, yes. It is from birth, it takes a capsule with the adapter, and it goes to 22 kg. It is worth thinking twice if you walk long distances daily on rough ground, where a larger wheel earns its keep.

faq.q: Will the Minu Duo fit through a standard doorway?
faq.a: Yes. The pram is {minuduo.width} wide and it is designed to clear a 73 cm doorway, which is the standard internal width in most Australian homes.

faq.q: Can I use the Minu Duo from birth?
faq.a: Yes, both seats, as sold. That is unusual in a double this compact. Most side-by-sides need one child to be sitting up before you can use both seats.

faq.q: Is the Minu Duo suitable for twins?
faq.a: Yes. Both seats are the same size, both recline, and both are usable from birth, so neither twin is in the lesser seat.

faq.q: Will a Minu Duo fit in my boot?
faq.a: Folded it is {minuduo.folded}. It is wide rather than long, so the number to check against your boot opening is the {minuduo.width_only} width.

faq.q: How heavy is the Minu Duo?
faq.a: {minuduo.weight}, which is around the weight of a single full-size pram for two seats.

faq.q: How much weight does each seat take?
faq.a: Up to {minuduo.to}, so it stays usable well into the toddler years for both children.

faq.q: How much can the basket hold?
faq.a: {minuduo.basket} across the one basket underneath.

faq.q: Are the Minu Duo seats reversible?
faq.a: No, both seats face forward. Side-by-side doubles are built this way so the frame stays narrow enough for a doorway.

faq.q: How is the Minu Duo different from a tandem double?
faq.a: A tandem is long, so it is harder in a lift and in a queue but narrower through a gap. The Minu Duo is the other trade: wider, but short, and both children get the same seat and the same view.

faq.q: Can I use the Ridge V2 from birth?
faq.a: Not as sold: it starts from six months. From birth it needs a bassinet or a capsule with the Ridge Mesa/bassinet adapters, both sold separately.

faq.q: Can I run with the Ridge V2?
faq.a: Yes, that is what it is built for. Never-flat tyres, a front wheel that locks straight for running and unlocks to swivel for walking, and the longest wheelbase we make, which is what keeps it stable at pace.

faq.q: Will a Ridge V2 fit in my boot?
faq.a: Folded it is {ridge.folded}, which is the largest fold in the range. It is a pram for families with boot space. Worth measuring before you commit.

faq.q: How heavy is the Ridge V2?
faq.a: {ridge.weight}. In its box it is 18.9 kg.

faq.q: Can the Ridge V2 carry two children?
faq.a: Yes, up to {ridge.children}, using a second seat or a ride-along board.

faq.q: What weight does the Ridge V2 take?
faq.a: From {ridge.from} to {ridge.to}, the highest limit in the range.

faq.q: Do the tyres need pumping up?
faq.a: No. They are never-flat, so there is no pump, no valve and no puncture on a gravel track.

faq.q: What is included with the Ridge V2?
faq.a: Never-flat tyres, the basket and basket cover, a bottle holder and the three year warranty.

faq.q: Is the Ridge V2 seat reversible?
faq.a: No, it faces forward. On a jogger that is deliberate. The child needs to see where they are going and the frame needs the length for stability.

faq.q: How wide is the Ridge V2?
faq.a: {ridge.width} across, opened out to {ridge.unfolded}.

faq.q: Is the Ridge V2 only useful if I run?
faq.a: No. The same tyres and wheelbase that suit running suit sand, grass, gravel and unsealed paths. If most of your walking is on footpaths, a Cruz or a Vista will be easier to store.

faq.q: How long is the warranty in Australia?
faq.a: Three years from purchase against manufacturing defects, plus complimentary maintenance checks for up to ten years under Lifetime Service Support. Register your pram to activate it.

faq.q: Is buying direct cheaper than a retailer?
faq.a: No, and deliberately so. Our prices match authorised retailers. Buying direct gets you genuine stock, the Australian warranty, four month lay-by and UPPside Rewards points.

faq.a: Airline damage is excluded from the standard warranty, as it is with every pram brand. Our TravelSafe Program covers it: buy an UPPAbaby travel bag, register before you fly, and you are covered for four years.

faq.q: Which UPPAbaby pram can I use from birth?
faq.a: Vista V3, Cruz V3, Minu V3 and Minu Duo are all suitable from birth as sold. Vista includes the bassinet in the box. Cruz and Minu include an infant insert and a from-birth recline. Minu Duo is from birth on both seats. Ridge V2 is the exception. It is a jogger, and it needs a bassinet or a Mesa capsule to be used before about six months. Kona is from birth with the bassinet or a Mesa capsule.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Vista and the Cruz?
faq.a: Vista carries up to three children and Cruz carries one. That is the decision. Both have the same seat quality, the same canopy and the same fabrics. Vista has a larger frame that accepts a second seat, a second bassinet or a PiggyBack board, and it ships with the bassinet included. Cruz is narrower and lighter and does not take a second seat at all. Vista is $1,799 and weighs 12.5 kg with the seat on. Cruz is $1,299 and weighs 12 kg. If one child is genuinely the plan, Cruz is the better buy and the smaller fold.

faq.q: Can a Vista carry two children?
faq.a: Yes. Vista V3 takes a second seat or a second bassinet on the same frame, and a PiggyBack board makes room for a third child to stand at the back. There are more than thirty configurations off the one frame. This is the reason Vista costs more than Cruz. If a second child is possible, Vista is the frame that absorbs it without you buying a second pram.

faq.q: Which pram is best for twins?
faq.a: Minu Duo. It is a side-by-side double with two equal-sized seats, both usable from birth, and it is narrow enough to clear a standard 73 cm doorway. Vista is also an option for twins using two bassinets or two seats, but it carries them one in front of the other rather than side by side, and it is a larger fold. Minu Duo is $1,299.

Minu V3, at 7.6 kg. It folds to 25 x 45 x 55 cm and stands on its own. It is the only model in the range that folds small enough to be treated as carry-on sized luggage, which is why it is the usual choice for families who fly.

faq.q: What is the difference between a pram and a stroller?
faq.a: In the UPPAbaby range, prams are the full-size frames with larger wheels, larger baskets and reversible or convertible seating: Vista, Cruz, Ridge and Kona. Strollers are the lighter, more compact frames built around a small fold: Minu V3 and Minu Duo. The words are used interchangeably in Australia, so the practical question is not what it is called but how big it is folded and how many children it carries. The comparison tool puts those side by side.

faq.q: Will an UPPAbaby pram fit in my boot?
faq.a: Measure the shortest side of your boot opening and compare it to the pram's folded height, which is the dimension that usually decides it. Folded with the seat attached: Minu V3 is 25 x 45 x 55 cm. Kona is 34 x 53.3 x 65.5 cm. Vista V3 is 41.4 x 65.3 x 85.9 cm. Cruz V3 is 43 x 57.2 x 82.3 cm. Minu Duo is 33 x 70.6 x 60.2 cm. Ridge V2 is 49.5 x 65 x 91.4 cm. Vista and Cruz both fold smaller again with the seat removed: Vista to 28.7 x 65.3 x 82.9 cm, Cruz to 34.3 x 57.2 x 76.9 cm. The boot fit tool does the comparison for you.

faq.q: How wide is the Minu Duo?
faq.a: The Minu Duo is 70.6 cm wide, and it is designed to fit through a standard 73 cm doorway. Those are two different measurements. The pram itself is 70.6 cm; the 73 cm figure is the doorway it clears.

faq.q: How much do UPPAbaby prams weigh?
faq.a: Minu V3 is 7.6 kg, Kona is 9.9 kg, Cruz V3 is 12 kg with the seat on, Vista V3 is 12.5 kg with the seat on, Minu Duo is 12.7 kg and Ridge V2 is 13.7 kg. Vista splits into a 9 kg frame and a 3.5 kg seat, which matters if you are lifting it into a high boot on your own.

faq.q: How long will my child fit in the pram?
faq.a: Vista V3, Cruz V3 and Kona take a child to 22.7 kg. Minu V3 takes a child to 22 kg. Minu Duo takes 22.7 kg per seat. In practice most children are out of a pram before they reach the weight limit, so seat height and legroom tend to matter more than the number.

faq.q: Does the Mesa capsule fit my UPPAbaby pram?
faq.a: The Mesa clicks directly onto Vista and Cruz with no adapters. It fits Minu V3, Minu Duo, Ridge V2 and Kona with the matching adapter set, sold separately. That means a sleeping baby moves from the car to the pram without being unbuckled, which is the single most useful thing a capsule does.

faq.a: The Mesa capsule is CASA approved for aircraft use. Prams are normally checked at the gate rather than carried on. Use a travel bag. faq.q: What the three year warranty covers
faq.a: Your UPPAbaby product is warranted to be free from manufacturing defects for three years from the date of purchase , under normal use and in line with the operating instructions. Three years applies to prams and strollers, bouncers, high chairs, playards, swings and bassinets, and to selected accessories: the RumbleSeat, the Changing Station and the PiggyBack. All other accessories carry two years against manufacturing defects on the same terms. The practical difference A warranty covers something that was wrong when the product was made. Service covers everything that happens afterwards, from a wheel that has developed a squeak at year four to a harness that needs re-tensioning. Most of what actually goes wrong with a pram over its life is the second kind, which is why we run both.

faq.q: What we do about a defect
faq.a: We supply replacement parts or carry out repairs, whichever we determine is appropriate. We may exchange an item for a replacement part, and some parts may be replaced with newer model parts as the product is improved over time.

We check and adjust the brakes, wheels, harness, fold mechanism and canopy, and tell you honestly what condition the pram is in. faq.q: Your rights under Australian Consumer Law
faq.a: This warranty sits on top of your rights under Australian Consumer Law. It does not replace them and cannot reduce them. Our goods come with guarantees that cannot be excluded under the Australian Consumer Law. You are entitled to a replacement or refund for a major failure, and to compensation for any other reasonably foreseeable loss or damage. You are also entitled to have the goods repaired or replaced if they fail to be of acceptable quality and the failure does not amount to a major failure. These guarantees apply for a reasonable period given the price and nature of the product, which for a pram at this price can be longer than three years.
